pairs: Sapiens mulier ædificat domum suam;
A wise woman builds up her household.
insipiens exstructam quoque manibus destruet.
But a foolish one will pull down with her own hands what has been built up.
Ambulans recto itinere,
One who walks on a virtuous journey,
et timens Deum,
and who fears God,
despicitur ab eo qui infami graditur via.
is despised by him who advances along a disreputable way.
In ore stulti virga superbiæ;
In the mouth of the foolish,
labia autem sapientium custodiunt eos.
there is a rod of arrogance. But the lips of the wise guard them.
Ubi non sunt boves,
Where there are no oxen,
præsepe vacuum est;
the feeding trough is empty.
ubi autem plurimæ segetes,
But where there are many crops,
ibi manifesta est fortitudo bovis.
there the strength of the ox is manifest.
Testis fidelis non mentitur;
A faithful witness will not lie.
profert autem mendacium dolosus testis.
But a deceitful witness offers a lie.
Quærit derisor sapientiam,
A mocker seeks wisdom
et non invenit;
and does not find it.
doctrina prudentium facilis.
The doctrine of the prudent is accessible.
Vade contra virum stultum,
Go against a foolish man,
et nescit labia prudentiæ.
and he does not acknowledge lips of prudence.
Sapientia callidi est intelligere viam suam,
The wisdom of a discerning man is to understand his way.
et imprudentia stultorum errans.
And the imprudence of the foolish is to be wandering astray.
Stultus illudet peccatum,
The foolish will speak mockingly of sin.
et inter justos morabitur gratia.
But grace lingers among the just.
Cor quod novit amaritudinem animæ suæ,
The heart that knows the bitterness of its own soul,
in gaudio ejus non miscebitur extraneus.
in its gladness the outsider shall not meddle.
Domus impiorum delebitur:
The house of the impious will be wiped away.
tabernacula vero justorum germinabunt.
Yet truly, the tabernacles of the just shall spring forth.
Est via quæ videtur homini justa,
There is a way which seems just to a man,
novissima autem ejus deducunt ad mortem.
but its conclusion leads to death.
Risus dolore miscebitur,
Laughter shall be mingled with sorrow,
et extrema gaudii luctus occupat.
and mourning occupies the limits of joy.
Viis suis replebitur stultus,
The foolish will be filled up by his own ways.
et super eum erit vir bonus.
And the good man shall be above him.
Innocens credit omni verbo;
The innocent trust every word.
astutus considerat gressus suos.
The astute one considers his own steps.
Filio doloso nihil erit boni;
Nothing good will be for the deceitful son.
servo autem sapienti prosperi erunt actus,
But the wise servant shall act prosperously
et dirigetur via ejus.
and his way will be set in order.
Sapiens timet,
The wise fear,
et declinat a malo;
and so turn away from evil.
stultus transilit, et confidit.
The foolish leap ahead with confidence.
Impatiens operabitur stultitiam,
The impatient will work foolishness.
et vir versutus odiosus est.
And a resourceful man is hated.
Possidebunt parvuli stultitiam,
The childish will possess foolishness,
et exspectabunt astuti scientiam.
and the discerning will anticipate knowledge.
Jacebunt mali ante bonos,
The evil will fall down before the good.
et impii ante portas justorum.
And the impious will fall down before the gates of the just.
Etiam proximo suo pauper odiosus erit:
The pauper will be hated, even by his own neighbor. Yet truly,
amici vero divitum multi.
the friends of the wealthy are many.
Qui despicit proximum suum peccat;
Whoever despises his neighbor, sins.
qui autem miseretur pauperis beatus erit.
But whoever pities the poor shall be blessed.
Qui credit in Domino misericordiam diligit.
Whoever trusts in the Lord loves mercy.
Errant qui operantur malum;
They wander astray who work evil.
misericordia et veritas præparant bona.
But mercy and truth prepare good things.
In omni opere erit abundantia;
In every work, there shall be abundance.
ubi autem verba sunt plurima,
But where there are many words,
ibi frequenter egestas.
there is often need.
Corona sapientium divitiæ eorum;
The crown of the wise is their wealth.
fatuitas stultorum imprudentia.
The senselessness of the foolish is imprudence.
Liberat animas testis fidelis,
A faithful witness frees souls.
et profert mendacia versipellis.
And the chameleon utters lies.
In timore Domini fiducia fortitudinis,
In the fear of the Lord is the faithfulness of strength,
et filiis ejus erit spes.
and there shall be hope for his sons.
Timor Domini fons vitæ,
The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life,
ut declinent a ruina mortis.
so as to turn aside from the ruin of death.
In multitudine populi dignitas regis,
In a multitude of people, there is dignity for the king.
et in paucitate plebis ignominia principis.
And in a paucity of people, there is disgrace for the prince.
Qui patiens est multa gubernatur prudentia;
Whoever is patient is governed by much prudence.
qui autem impatiens est exaltat stultitiam suam.
But whoever is impatient exalts his foolishness.
Vita carnium sanitas cordis;
The well-being of the heart is life for the flesh.
putredo ossium invidia.
But envy is decay for the bones.
Qui calumniatur egentem exprobrat factori ejus;
Whoever slanders the indigent argues against his Maker.
honorat autem eum qui miseretur pauperis.
But he who has compassion on the poor honors his Maker.
In malitia sua expelletur impius:
The impious will be expelled in his malice.
sperat autem justus in morte sua.
But the just finds hope even in his own death.
In corde prudentis requiescit sapientia,
In the heart of the prudent, wisdom finds rest.
et indoctos quosque erudiet.
And so shall he instruct all the uneducated.
Justitia elevat gentem;
Justice elevates a nation.
miseros autem facit populos peccatum.
But sin makes the peoples miserable.
Acceptus est regi minister intelligens;
An intelligent minister is acceptable to the king.
iracundiam ejus inutilis sustinebit.
Whoever is useless shall bear his wrath.
